text: A 2.1 failure that works on TestFlight but fails in review is commonly attributed (community answer, Mar 2026) to hardcoded IPv4 literals or raw BSD sockets on the IPv6-only review network; use hostnames and URLSession/Network framework, and reproduce with an Internet Sharing NAT64 network. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-01)

text: Guideline 2.3.1 prohibits hidden, dormant or undocumented features and requires new functionality to be described specifically in Notes for Review; generic descriptions are rejected. An optional user-keyed AI feature or Slack/SMTP alerting that a reviewer cannot trigger must be documented there. (medium confidence)
keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

text: If a demo account cannot be supplied for legal or security reasons, 2.1 allows a built-in demo mode that shows full functionality, with prior Apple approval. For optional features needing user-supplied credentials, the safe pattern is that the core app works with none and the optional feature has a clearly labelled, documented off state. (medium confidence)
keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

text: Apple does not publish App Review source IP ranges; blog reports of Cupertino or Sacramento ranges are unconfirmed and change, so allowlisting or geo/IP gating a backend is an antipattern for review. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-01)
keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

text: Guideline 2.5.5 requires apps to be fully functional on IPv6-only networks, and Apple DTS states App Review tests on an IPv6-only network with DNS64/NAT64 (ARNAT64), which now behaves much like MacNAT64 (Internet Sharing based) rather than a carrier network. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

text: Guideline 2.1 tells developers to submit final builds, include demo account info if the app has a login, and turn on the back-end service so it is live and accessible during review; non-obvious features must be explained in Review Notes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

text: Apple staff caution that a rejection message citing IPv6 may have nothing to do with the network; crashes during review are bugs regardless of network state. Treat the network as one hypothesis, not the diagnosis. (high confidence)
